skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-customer-match
skill.description: Guide WooCommerce merchants through Google Ads Customer Match setup with Product Metrics. Check prerequisites and consent settings, then verify that the six audience lists exist.
skill.summary: Set up and verify six Google Ads Customer Match audiences for WooCommerce.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags are Markdown, documentation links, or normal application checks. The skill does direct authenticated writes and order reads and advertises an unpinned installer. The review found insufficient approval guidance for order imports, conflicting hashing statements, and unrelated credential exceptions, but no evidence of malicious intent or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Prerequisite setup can import existing orders and extend data sharing beyond Google Ads.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a read-only check. Before any write or import, disclose the exact store, workspace, account, data, and recipients. Require separate approval for additional channels.

remediation.issue: Customer Match documentation gives conflicting descriptions of hashing.
remediation.suggestion: List which fields are hashed and which remain unhashed. Show that disclosure before list creation and distinguish Customer Match from conversion tracking.

remediation.issue: The rules allow unrelated channel credentials to pass through agent commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove those exceptions from this skill. Direct users to enter credentials in the vendor interface or an approved secret manager.

remediation.issue: Order verification uses general order reads for a narrow customer classification check.
remediation.suggestion: Limit reads to the authorized store and requested test orders. Return only the new or returning classification rather than full order details.

remediation.issue: The documented install invokes a package runner and references an unpinned skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Pin and verify the installer version and upstream commit. Present installation as a separate, user-approved action.

remediation.issue: Missing local references are replaced by mutable remote instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references. When they are missing, treat remote content as informational and require independent approval before following steps that change state.

semantic_findings.title: Prerequisite Setup Broadens Order Data Sharing
semantic_findings.description: The workflow points merchants to tracking setup if it is missing. That guide queues existing orders and presents Meta and ChatGPT Ads alongside Google Ads. It does not separate approval for that broader sharing from the Customer Match request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly includes an initial order import and additional channels. The steps are visible to merchants, but the guide does not distinguish those permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Disclosure of Customer Match Data
semantic_findings.description: The guide identifies country and postcode as unhashed but later says everything is hashed. A merchant could approve audience syncing with an inaccurate understanding of which fields Google receives in clear form.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The field table and the hashing statement directly conflict. The documentation establishes the inconsistency, not the actual payload sent by the service.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Channel Credential Exceptions
semantic_findings.description: The rules allow agents to take Lightspeed, Meta, or OpenAI credentials from a user and pass them into a command. None is required for WooCommerce Customer Match, and direct command handling may expose credentials to tooling or process inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exceptions are explicit and absent from the workflow prerequisites. The record does not show an actual credential request or exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Documentation Replaces Reviewed Instructions
semantic_findings.description: When local references are missing, the skill treats live vendor Markdown as equivalent to the bundled steps. The same workflow follows those steps to completion, so later document changes could alter what the agent recommends or does.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The conditional substitution is explicit and specifies no version or integrity check. There is no evidence that the current remote content contains malicious instructions.

content.user_title: Set Up WooCommerce Customer Match in Google Ads
content.value_statement: WooCommerce merchants need to connect several services before they can use order-based audiences in Google Ads. This skill checks the setup and guides you through creating six Customer Match lists with Product Metrics.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP service and identify completed prerequisites.
Guide merchants through WordPress plugin and Google Ads setup when a connection is missing.
Explain how to configure a supported consent banner before enabling audience membership.
Guide merchants through creating or completing the six Customer Match lists in Product Metrics.
Check whether a WooCommerce test order was recognized as new or returning and explain how to verify lists in Google Ads.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a connected WooCommerce store, and an eligible Google Ads setup with Merchant Center.
The account operator must accept Google Ads terms and make any campaign or bidding changes.
Existing customers are not added in bulk. Membership can begin with a later eligible paid order.
Unsupported or unconfigured consent banners do not provide the consent needed for list membership.

use_cases.title: Plan existing customer exclusions
use_cases.description: Prepare the All customers list and confirm when it can be used to exclude buyers from acquisition campaigns.

use_cases.title: Review audiences for a win-back campaign
use_cases.description: Check whether the Lapsed customers list exists and understand when it gains members before applying it in Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Verify order recognition and consent
use_cases.description: Check a test order, confirm the consent banner configuration, and identify which setup steps still need an account operator.

prompt_templates.title: Review prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan the setup without account changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me a Customer Match setup checklist for my WooCommerce store. Explain what I need in WordPress, Product Metrics, and Google Ads.

prompt_templates.title: Check current setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Product Metrics setup without making changes. Tell me which Customer Match prerequisites are complete and which steps I need to perform.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose empty lists
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate lists that have no members.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose empty Customer Match lists. Check consent and paid order settings, and tell me how to verify one test order without showing customer identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Review an audience rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare an approval checklist for one store.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the selected WooCommerce store and Google Ads account. Identify which lists are missing and what data is shared. Stop before writes, imports, or campaign changes.

output_examples.input: What is left to do before creating Customer Match lists?
output_examples.output: WooCommerce is connected and tracking is active. Verify your supported consent banner and accept the Customer Match terms in Google Ads. No lists were created.

output_examples.input: The lists exist. Why are they empty?
output_examples.output: Existing customers are not added in bulk. After a paid order with both required consent signals, check Google Ads for list membership.

output_examples.input: Was my test order from a returning buyer?
output_examples.output: Product Metrics classified the selected test order as returning. No customer identifiers or margin values are included here.

best_practices: Confirm the exact WooCommerce store, Product Metrics workspace, and Google Ads client account before changing settings.
Verify that the supported banner supplies both required consent signals and clear the full-page cache after a configuration change.
Review data fields and destinations before approving an import or creating audiences. Start verification with one test order.
anti_patterns: Paste a WordPress setup token, an API key, or customer billing details into the assistant chat.
Assume a historical order import will populate Customer Match lists with existing customers.
Enable unrelated ad channels or change campaign bidding as part of a Customer Match check.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics Pro?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide requires Pro with Full Signal Tracking and workspace administrator access for Customer Match setup.

faq.question: Which consent banners are supported?
faq.answer: The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano. If consent cannot be read, customers do not join the lists.

faq.question: Will customers from past orders appear automatically?
faq.answer: No. Customers can join after their next eligible paid order once the lists exist.

faq.question: Which WooCommerce orders count as paid?
faq.answer: The plugin uses the statuses you select under Orders & product data. Processing and Completed are common choices.

faq.question: Are guest orders included?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics uses the billing email or phone number for guests. A later order under a customer account starts a separate history.

faq.question: Will the setup change campaigns in Google Ads?
faq.answer: No. It creates and maintains lists. You decide whether to use them as campaign exclusions or audience signals.
